statement.summary: Theorem 6.3 is frozen as two Props: (i) `upperUnionStatement`, an inequality in ℕ with the right side abbreviated `unionRHS` (sum over `n.primeFactors` of `gaussBinom p d 1 * σ^(n^d/p)`), and (ii) `upperClosedStatement`, an inequality in ℝ with the prefactor `closedPrefactor n d = 2^d − 1 + 2·logb 2 n` and the real power σ^(N/2). `upperBoundsStatement` is their conjunction.
deltas: Alphabet Σ is `Fin σ`; |S_{n^d}| is `numSS n d σ` (`Nat.card` of the shift-symmetric configurations).
`p ∣ n` in the sums ranges over the prime divisors `n.primeFactors`.
[d 1]_p is the q-Pascal `gaussBinom p d 1`, equal to the paper's product formula for p ≥ 2 by the separately frozen and proved `gaussProdEqStatement`.
(i): the exponent n^d/p is ℕ-division, exact since p | n^d; the inequality is in ℕ.
(ii): the inequality is in ℝ; log₂ = `Real.logb 2`; σ^{n^d/2} is the real power with real exponent N/2 (not ℕ-division, which would make the statement stronger than the paper's for odd N).

maps.label: Theorem 6.3 = (i) ∧ (ii)
maps.note: The theorem is the conjunction of the two frozen Props, one per enumerated item.

maps.label: n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1, σ ≥ 2
maps.note: Same hypotheses in both parts, verbatim. (The Lean proof of (i) uses only n ≥ 2: the union bound holds for every σ and d.)

maps.label: alphabet Σ with |Σ| = σ
maps.note: Σ is `Fin σ`; only |Σ| enters the count, so this is a relabeling.

maps.label: (i) |S_{n^d}| ≤ Σ_{p|n} [d 1]_p σ^{n^d/p}

lean.text: numSS n d σ ≤ unionRHS n d σ

maps.note: Inequality of natural numbers; the right side is the abbreviation `unionRHS`.

maps.label: |S_{n^d}|

lean.text: Nat.card {s : Config n d (Fin σ) // IsShiftSymmetric s}
∃ v : Lat n d, v ≠ 0 ∧ shift v s = s

maps.note: |S_{n^d}| = `numSS`: `Nat.card` of the shift-symmetric configurations (some nonzero translation fixes s, i.e. Stab(s) ≠ {0}).

maps.label: Σ_{p|n} [d 1]_p σ^{n^d/p}

lean.text: ∑ p ∈ n.primeFactors, gaussBinom p d 1 * σ ^ (n ^ d / p)

maps.note: The sum term by term; see the sub-maps for the index set, the binomial and the exponent.

maps.label: Σ over primes p | n
maps.note: `p ∣ n` in the paper ranges over prime divisors (it is the p of 𝓛_p); Lean sums over `n.primeFactors`.

maps.label: [d 1]_p

lean.text: gaussProd q d r = (gaussBinom q d r : ℚ)

maps.note: The paper defines [d r]_p by the product formula; Lean uses the q-Pascal recursion `gaussBinom`. They agree for q ≥ 2 (`gaussProdEqStatement`, proved separately as `gaussProdEq_proved`).

maps.label: σ^{n^d/p}
maps.note: `n ^ d / p` is ℕ-division; it is exact because p | n | n^d (d ≥ 1), so no truncation.

maps.label: (ii) |S_{n^d}| ≤ (2^d − 1 + 2 log₂ n) σ^{n^d/2}

lean.text: (numSS n d σ : ℝ) ≤ closedPrefactor n d * (σ : ℝ) ^ (((n ^ d : ℕ) : ℝ) / 2)

maps.note: Inequality in ℝ (the prefactor contains a logarithm and the exponent can be a half-integer).

maps.label: |S_{n^d}| cast to ℝ
maps.note: Same count `numSS` as in (i), cast ℕ → ℝ (cast is exact).

maps.label: 2^d − 1 + 2 log₂ n
maps.note: The prefactor is the real number `closedPrefactor n d`; 2^d − 1 is computed in ℝ (no truncated subtraction).

maps.label: log₂ n
maps.note: log₂ is mathlib's `Real.logb 2` applied to the real cast of n (n ≥ 2, so the argument is positive).

maps.label: σ^{n^d/2} as a real power
maps.note: Real power (`Real.rpow`) with the real exponent N/2. For odd N, ℕ-division would truncate the exponent to (N−1)/2 and assert a STRONGER inequality than the paper; the real power is the literal reading.
